notes: The parts are the same as in step 1. Nothing was added or dropped.

Fix for the validator error: the catalogue's antenna port rp-sma has kind 'socket', and my first draft gave the board's antenna port kind 'header-socket', which is not a compatible pair. The board's antenna port is now kind 'ball', which does pair with a socket. Real hardware has a u.FL connector there. 'ball' is only the closest allowed kind and is not meant literally.
The MKR WAN 1310 is not in the catalogue or on the shop sites, so a new type arduino-mkr-wan-1310 is defined. Its pin names follow the labels in the circuit images (DAC0/A0 is named A0).

Sender: GND on the MKR goes through the black wire to one side of the pushbutton. Pin 2 goes through the yellow wire to the other side. The code uses INPUT_PULLUP, so no external resistor is needed, and pressing the button pulls pin 2 to GND. The button is placed across the breadboard's centre gap with its two sides in columns 5 and 6. The image draws it in one half of the board, so the exact holes are my approximation.

Receiver: pin 2 goes through the green wire and the resistor to the LED anode. The LED cathode goes through the black wire to GND. The LED's bent (longer) leg in the image is taken as the anode. The resistor is on the anode side as the image shows.
The resistor value is not given in the tutorial. 220 ohm is assumed.
Each antenna is attached to its board's u.FL connector by its own cable, so there are no separate jumper wires for it.
The USB cables are not drawn in the diagrams. They are joined to the boards' micro-USB ports only, with no electrical edge, since the cable has no ports in the catalogue.
